fields.display_title: Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 5LSi
fields.replying_to: Replying to Achieving Olympia-Level Geometry Large Language Model Agent via Complexity Boosting Reinforcement Learning

fields.display_title: 1. Does Pass@256 with 200 steps implies ~51K LLM–engine interactions per problem? Does this raise scalability and efficiency concerns.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 5LSi

fields.display_title: 7. How crucial are the additions of "dynamic diagram adjustment" and "double points" handling for solving the IMO-level problems? Will be good if authors can add this to improve the quality of the paper.
fields.replying_to: Replying to 1. Does Pass@256 with 200 steps implies ~51K LLM–engine interactions per problem? Does this raise scalability and efficiency concerns.

fields.display_title: 2. The paper does not report inference time per problem or single-shot success rate (Pass@1); it will make the paper better if we have this presented so we can assess the model’s true reasoning efficiency.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 5LSi

fields.display_title: 3. Would be nice if authors can add a baseline between the pretrained InternThinker-32B and the CBRL-trained InternGeometry, this will make it clear on how much improvement gain from CBRL does the proposed method have.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 5LSi

fields.display_title: 4. Although case studies are insightful, a deeper analysis of failure cases (the unsolved problems in Table 2) or reasoning trajectories would provide better understanding. Authors can add this qualitative analysis in the draft, which will make the readability better.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 5LSi

fields.display_title: 5. Will be great if the paper can mention inference/training compute requirements to reproduce the results. This will help in reproducibility.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 5LSi

fields.display_title: 6. To justify InterGeometry's generalization capabilities, authors may want to include an analysis of the cross-domain performance on mathematical and scientific reasoning tasks, which can improve the usefulness of the paper.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 5LSi

fields.display_title: 8. As mentioned in Equation (9) add a brief explanation of how maximizing "absolute advantage" creates a curriculum of moderate difficulty and how the search for ‘k’ is done in each round.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 5LSi

fields.display_title: 9. The paper builds upon InternThinker-32B as the foundation for InternGeometry model. However, the current version lacks sufficient details about InternThinker-32B’s architecture, training setup, and reasoning capabilities. Hope authors can add this to the draft and improve the paper quality.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 5LSi

fields.display_title: 10. Also, please clarify what aspects of InternThinker-32B enable effective long-horizon reasoning and symbolic interaction in this work.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 5LSi

fields.display_title: Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 2RDT
fields.replying_to: Replying to Achieving Olympia-Level Geometry Large Language Model Agent via Complexity Boosting Reinforcement Learning

fields.display_title: 1. While the RL reward and RL loss are clearly defined, the handling and explanation of the curriculum algorithm lacks clarity, which makes it hard to evaluate the soundness of the proposed curriculum approach.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 2RDT

fields.display_title: 2. Data curation for cold-start requires clarity
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 2RDT

fields.display_title: 3. Could you provide a simplified high-level pseudocode for the working implementation of CBRL so the selection of the curriculum complexity  becomes clear, as well as explaining the technical challenges of implementing the CBRL algorithm? This would greatly benefit the soundness and clarity of the RL training done in this paper.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 2RDT

fields.display_title: 4. A cost comparison between deploying InternGeometry versus AlphaGeometry or SeedGeometry would be greatly valuable for this work. I understand this might or might not be feasible based on the information available from the prior work, but it would be interesting to compare the number of interaction steps between the deductive engine and the LLM with the prior work. Especially since the LLM usage for proposing propositions might greatly improve the interaction efficiency as well.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer 2RDT

fields.display_title: Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer YNAr
fields.replying_to: Replying to Achieving Olympia-Level Geometry Large Language Model Agent via Complexity Boosting Reinforcement Learning

fields.display_title: 1. The paper would benefit from more discussion regarding inference-time costs of the compared methods. For example, listing the model sizes in Table 1 would be helpful, as well as explaining the different search parameters in AlphaGeometry2’s custom beam search. If available, information about the total # of output tokens or wallclock time etc. would also be appreciated.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer YNAr

fields.display_title: 7. Should the top-left cell of Table 1 say “AlphaGeometry2” instead of “AlphaGeometry”?
fields.replying_to: Replying to 1. The paper would benefit from more discussion regarding inference-time costs of the compared methods. For example, listing the model sizes in Table 1 would be helpful, as well as explaining the different search parameters in AlphaGeometry2’s custom beam search. If available, information about the total # of output tokens or wallclock time etc. would also be appreciated.

fields.display_title: 2. Similarly, I think it would be nice if the paper also discussed training costs and compared them with previous methods. Currently, it mentions the size of the training set, but other information would also be helpful, such as the total # of tokens in the training set and a version of Figure 4 where the x-axis is the number of training tokens.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer YNAr

fields.display_title: 3. The writing quality is poor: - There are many grammatical mistakes and unidiomatic uses of English, including in the title and abstract. I recommend using something like ChatGPT to improve the writing. - There are missing citations (e.g., the last two paragraphs of the introduction section have no citations) - Other miscellaneous issues, e.g., labeling imprecise claims as “theorems” (lines 247-251), potential typos in Eq. (5), and missing explanations( what’s “split” in Table 2?)
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer YNAr

fields.display_title: 4. What is InternThinker-32B? There is no citation, and I couldn’t find any information about it on the Internet.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer YNAr

fields.display_title: 5. How are Eqs. (5) and (6) different from GRPO? (other than what appears to be typos)
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer YNAr

fields.display_title: 6. How is CBRL different from RL with a curriculum?
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer YNAr

fields.display_title: 8. The claim that InternGeometry’s test-time scaling budget is “far lower than that of AlphaGeometry2” (lines 311-312) is not clear to me. InternGeometry does pass@256 and uses a larger model (32B instead of 3.3B), so it’s not clear that it uses "far less" computational resources than AlphaGeometry2.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission22487 by Reviewer YNAr
